meta.notes: CRITICAL FINDING: The current dataset contains ZERO bechina edges for reference===73. All three existing edges for Torah 73 are of type 'eitza'. Therefore there are no bechina-connected components to derive from the dataset. All packages below are constructed entirely from the gap analysis of the source text (step 7), which identified 12+ bechina-language statements using the markers נִקְרָא, הוּא, and הַיְנוּ. Per the framework, every bechina-connected node must appear in exactly one package — since there are no dataset nodes, all nodes listed are proposed additions. Small isolated clusters (Yud/machshava, Aleph/tzaddik, Nukva, Torah/water) are merged into thematically nearest packages based on shared nature.

packages.label: כְּלִי אֲנִי — אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתְּפִלָּה
packages.label_en: The Vessel Ani — The Letters of Prayer
packages.reason: This is the central conceptual cluster of Torah #73. The Rebbe builds one continuous bechina chain: every Jew is called a tzaddik (נִקְרָא צַדִּיק), the tzaddik is called Aleph (נִקְרָא אָלֶף); the Nun is called speech (נִקְרָא דִּבּוּר), speech IS malkhut (הַדִּבּוּר הוּא מַלְכוּת), malkhut IS called Nun (נִקְרָא נוּן); thought IS called Yud (הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נִקְרָא יוּד); and the completed vessel IS called Ani (הַכְּלִי הַנִּקְרָא אֲנִי). These are all parallel aspects of the same essential structure: the three letters א-נ-י that form the word 'Ani' (I), each letter encoding a faculty of the person in prayer — the righteous soul (aleph), the speech/dibur/malkhut (nun), and the thought/intention (yud). They are different expressions of the same underlying reality: the formation of a receiving vessel for divine abundance through united conscious prayer. The 'mouth/peh' identity of malkhut is a further aspect of the same dibur cluster. Aleph, tzaddik, and ישראל are merged here because 'every Jew is called tzaddik' is the explicit bechina introduction to the aleph identity — they share the same nature as the human pole of the prayer-vessel construction.

merge_notes.reason: The Yud is called thought (הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נִקְרָא יוּד) and thought is one of the three letters forming the vessel Ani. Though a 2-node isolated cluster in raw terms, its essential nature is inseparable from the letter-formation of Ani — it is the yud-component of the same vessel. Merged into Package 1 rather than standing alone.

ישראל, צדיק, and אלף form a 3-node chain: every Jew is called tzaddik, every tzaddik is called Aleph. These three concepts share one nature: the human actor who forms the Aleph-component of the vessel Ani. ישראל is the empirical referent, צדיק is the identity declared, and אלף is the letter-dimension of that identity. All are aspects of the same bechina in this Torah.

Malkhut = peh (mouth) is stated as an equation in the text ('מַלְכוּת – פֶּה'). Peh is another name for dibur-malkhut in this Torah, the Nun-component of Ani. It shares the essential nature of the dibur/malkhut/nun cluster already in this package.

packages.label: סְתִים וְגַלְיָא — פְּנִימִיּוּת וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת
packages.label_en: Hidden and Revealed — Inner and Outer
packages.reason: The Torah opens with a fundamental ontological duality that applies equally to Torah and to God: both are simultaneously hidden (stim/penimit) and revealed (galya/chitzoniut). What is revealed IS the garment and the external dimension (מַה שֶּׁנִּגְלֶה לָנוּ הוּא הַלְּבוּשׁ וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת); what is hidden IS the internal dimension (מַה שֶּׁנִּסְתָּר הוּא הַפְּנִימִיּוּת). These are bechina pairs: revealed=garment=external, hidden=inner. This is the structural frame of the entire Torah — the goal is to reach penimit through the tefila/vessel method. The polarity is neutral because this duality is a cosmic structural feature (not inherently good or evil in itself) — both Torah and God contain both dimensions, and the distinction applies symmetrically to the positive teaching.

packages.label: מַיִם וְתוֹרָה — הִתְגַּלּוּת
packages.reason: Two bechina statements converge in the verse interpretation at the end of the Torah: (1) 'water' IS Torah — וְאֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (a standard rabbinic bechina, Bava Kama 17a); (2) the word 'tavar' (תַּעֲבֹר) IS the language of revelation (מִלְּשׁוֹן הִתְגַּלּוּת), as Targum Onkelos renders it. These three concepts — מים, תורה, התגלות — share a single nature in this Torah's argument: they are the medium through which the hidden becomes accessible. When you 'pass through the water' (= when you desire that the Torah's hidden dimension be revealed to you), you need the vessel Ani. Torah/water and hitgalut are the domain of what is sought; the vessel Ani is the means. Polarity is neutral because Torah and revelation are cosmic structures, not inherently polarized in this teaching.

merge_notes.reason: מים and תורה form a 2-node bechina pair (Bava Kama 17a; used explicitly in verse interpretation). התגלות is a 1-node isolated concept (the meaning of 'tavar' per Onkelos) but shares the same essential nature: in this Torah, Torah, water, and revelation are all expressions of the same thing — the medium of divine presence that becomes accessible. Per framework, 1-2 node isolated concepts are merged into thematically nearest package based on shared nature.

packages.label: נוּקְבָא — קַבָּלַת תַּעֲנוּג
packages.reason: The Rebbe introduces a distinct bechina domain: whoever receives pleasure from another IS called 'Nukva' (נִקְרָא נוּקְבָא, i.e. the feminine/receptive pole). When God receives pleasure from Israel's prayers (reakh nikoakh), God becomes, as it were, Nukva relative to Israel. The verse 'נְקֵבָה תְּסוֹבֵב גָּבֶר' confirms the inversion: the inner/penimit becomes the outer/chitzoniut. The 'feminine' pole here is not the evil/negative dimension but the holy receptive dimension — it is the 'secret of isha' (בְּסוֹד אִשָּׁה) in the positive sense. This cluster is distinct from Package 1 (vessel formation) because it describes the divine response to the vessel, not the construction of the vessel. It is the telos/outcome of the tefila rather than its structure. Polarity is good because this is the holy dimension of divine receptivity — the Shechina receiving Israel.

merge_notes.reason: אישה and ריח ניחוח are both 1-node isolated bechina concepts. The Rebbe states that through the ריח ניחוח God receives (מְקַבֵּל) from Israel's prayers and thereby becomes 'בְּסוֹד אִשָּׁה' — in the secret of isha/woman. Isha and ריח ניחוח are the concrete names for the Nukva-state when God is the receiver. They share the essential nature of the Nukva cluster and are merged here per the framework rule on isolated 1-2 node components.
